newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM declines comment it may sell Northwest stake.
newsitem.headline: KLM declines comment it may sell Northwest stake.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Friday it was in talks with U.S. partner Northwest Airlines to try to resolve a boardroom battle over share ownership and to clinch a multi-year partnership agreement.
But a KLM spokesman refused to confirm or deny that the talks could lead to KLM divesting its 18.8 percent Northwest stake in exchange for a five to ten-year partnership deal.

"(KLM controller Herman) Bruggink told analysts in Geneva that we were in talks to try to come to an agreement on long-term contracts and that Northwest wanted to see the dispute between shareholders resolved," Peter Wellhuner said.
Until now, KLM's highly lucrative but often stormy partnership with Northwest has been based on a series of one-year contracts.
Longer-term contracts would enable the two to take the necessary financial risks to deepen the alliance.
Dutch media reported on Friday that Bruggink had hinted KLM might dispose of its Northwest stake if the two carriers finally reached agreement on operating contracts of five to ten years.
But Wellhuner said Bruggink had said only that he was hopeful the talks would yield a result.
"Of course one cannot rule anything out but KLM is adamant that it does not want to anticipate the outcome of these talks in any way," Wellhuner said.

KLM recently won the go-ahead from a Delaware Chancery court to pursue its legal challenge of a Northwest shareholder rights plan which would prevent KLM from exercising a 1998 option to increase its Northwest stake by five percent.
